rules: State: default, focus, error, disabled
Default to the country of the account
Accept pasted numbers with the + prefix and set the country from them
Store in E.164 (+40712345678); show it formatted for the country
Ask for a phone number only when it is used, and say what for in the hint
a11y: The country list is searchable by country name and code; arrow keys move, Enter picks
The number input uses type="tel" and autocomplete="tel"
The country trigger has an aria-label ("Country code, Romania +40")
Phone Input.code: react-phone-number-input (libphonenumber-js) with a shadcn Popover + Command country list.

Date Input.summary: A date people type in day, month and year segments, with a calendar button that opens Date Picker.
use: Known dates: birth date, invoice date, contract start, document expiry
Dates far from today, where typing is faster than paging months
Data entry forms used all day
avoid: Dates near today or with availability: use Date Picker
A period with a start and an end: use Date Range Picker
A time of day: use Time Picker
anatomy: Day, month and year segments in the locale order, with separators
Empty segments: DD, MM, YYYY in muted
Calendar button: calendar icon, opens Date Picker
rules: State: default, focus, error, disabled
Segment order and separators follow the locale (12.11.2026 for ro-RO)
Arrow keys change the focused segment; typing a full segment moves to the next
Validate on blur; errors name the rule: "Date must be after 1 Jan 2026"
Pasting a full date fills all segments
a11y: Each segment is a spinbutton with a label ("Day", "Month", "Year") inside a group labelled by the Field
The calendar button has aria-label="Choose date" and returns focus to the field on close
Errors are linked with aria-describedby
Date Input.code: react-aria DateField (segments) + shadcn Popover with Calendar (react-day-picker).

Duration Input.summary: A length of time in hours and minutes for time entries, SLAs, reminders and meeting length.
use: Time entries and timesheets
SLAs and response targets
Reminders and meeting length
avoid: A time of day: use Time Picker
A date: use Date Input or Date Picker
A count without a time unit: use Number Input
rules: State: default, focus, error
Accept "1:30", "90" (minutes) and "1.5h"; normalize on blur
Minutes above 59 roll into hours
Add a days segment only when the task needs it (lead times)
Store minutes as one number; errors name the limit ("Up to 24 h per entry")
a11y: Hours and minutes are inputs with labels ("Hours", "Minutes") in a group labelled by the Field
inputmode="numeric"; arrow keys step by 1
The normalized value is read back after blur ("1 hour 30 minutes")
Duration Input.code: custom: two shadcn Inputs (inputmode numeric) with unit addons; parse and normalize on blur, store minutes.

Address Autocomplete.summary: Address field with suggestions as people type; a pick fills the address fields below it.
use: Shipping and billing addresses at checkout
Company and customer addresses
Delivery or meeting places
avoid: Picking from a known list (a warehouse, an office): use Select or Combobox
Countries or cities only: use Combobox
Coordinates on a map: use Map
anatomy: Suggestions (Show suggestions): map-pin, street and number, then city and country on a second line
rules: Suggestions after 3 characters, with a debounce
A pick fills the separate fields below (street, city, postal code, country); people can still edit them
Keep what was typed if nothing matches, and offer manual entry
"Enter the address manually" opens the separate fields
Bias suggestions to the country of the account; show at most 5
a11y: Combobox pattern: role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant on the input
Arrow keys move through suggestions, Enter picks, Esc closes and keeps the text
The number of suggestions is announced politely
Address Autocomplete.code: shadcn Popover + Command (cmdk, shouldFilter=false) fed by a places API (Google Places, Mapbox), debounced.

Select Option.summary: A rich option in a Select, Combobox or Menu list: icon or avatar, title, a muted second line and a check when selected.
use: Options that share a name (two customers called Northwind)
Options a picture tells apart: workspaces, integrations, people
Lists where the type or place helps the choice
avoid: Short options that are clear by name: use Menu Item
People with role and email: use Person Option in People Picker
Choices with a long description: use Option Card
anatomy: Leading: icon tile or avatar (Leading, Icon)
rules: Leading: icon, avatar, none; the same Leading for every option in one list
State: default, highlighted
Description is one short line: type, place, email ("Customer · Berlin")
Title and description truncate on one line each; the full text shows in a tooltip
Checked marks the selected option; multi-select lists keep it open while picking
a11y: role="option" with aria-selected; the list is a listbox
Title and description are read together as the option name
Icons and avatars are decorative (aria-hidden) unless they carry meaning
Select Option.code: shadcn CommandItem or SelectItem with an Avatar or icon, two text lines and a check icon.

Recurrence Picker.summary: How often something repeats: interval and unit, the days or the day, when it ends, and a summary sentence.
use: Recurring invoices
Reports sent by email on a schedule
Reminders and meetings
avoid: One date: use Date Picker
A fixed set of choices (daily, weekly digest): use Select or Radio
A time of day only: use Time Picker
anatomy: Repeat every: interval Number Input and unit Select (day, week, month)
Days (Frequency=weekly): Toggle Group Items M T W T F S S
Summary (Show summary): "Every week on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, until 31 Dec 2026"
rules: Frequency: daily, weekly, monthly
The summary says the result in words; read it back in confirmations and lists
Weekly needs at least one day; default to the day of the start date
Monthly on day 29-31 says what happens in shorter months ("last day of the month")
Time zone of the account unless the field says otherwise
a11y: Each part has a label; Ends is a radiogroup
Day toggles have full names as aria-labels ("Monday") and aria-pressed
The summary is in a live region (aria-live="polite") so changes are read
Recurrence Picker.code: custom: Number Input, shadcn Select, ToggleGroup (type multiple) and RadioGroup; rrule for the rule and the summary.

File Field.summary: One file as a form field: Choose file, then the name and size, with remove.
use: One document in a form: a contract, a certificate
A logo or a CSV to import, where a dropzone is too big
Dense forms and Sheets
avoid: Several files or drag and drop: use File Dropzone with File Items
An avatar or a logo with a preview: use Avatar Upload
A file already in the product: use Select or Combobox
anatomy: Empty text "No file chosen" or the file name and size
Remove (x), once a file is chosen
rules: State: empty, selected, error
Accepted types and max size go in the Field hint
The error says what to change: "Choose a PDF under 10 MB."
Long file names truncate in the middle and keep the extension
Choosing a new file replaces the old one
a11y: A native input type="file" with a visible label through Field
Remove has an aria-label with the file name ("Remove contract-northwind.pdf")
Errors are linked with aria-describedby and announced
File Field.code: custom: hidden input type="file" + shadcn Button, file name and remove Button; react-hook-form for validation.

Swatch.summary: One choice of a color or a short label: a color dot (Type=color) or a box with a label like S, M, L (Type=label), with selected and unavailable states.
use: Colors in Swatch Picker (Size=sm)
Product colors and sizes on a product page (Size=default)
Material or finish choices
avoid: Any color, typed or picked freely: use Color Picker
Options with a price or a description: use Option Card
Long lists of options: use Select
anatomy: Color: a dot filled with a token or the product color (Type=color)
Ring when State=selected; faded when unavailable
rules: Override the fill of the "color" layer with a chart, brand or product color token, never a raw hex in the library
Group swatches under a label that names the choice and the value ("Color: Sand")
Unavailable options stay visible and focusable, faded, with "out of stock" in their name
Size=sm (28) in pickers, default (36) for product options
a11y: A radio group: each swatch is a radio with the color or option name as its label
Selected is announced; unavailable has aria-disabled and stays in the tab order
The ring has 3:1 contrast on light and dark backgrounds
Swatch.code: shadcn RadioGroup (or ToggleGroup type="single") with custom items: a color dot or a label box.

Swatch Picker.summary: A short set of colors for labels, categories, calendars and project avatars, with the name of the selected one.
use: Label and tag colors
Calendar and category colors
Project or workspace avatar colors
avoid: Any color (brand, themes): use Color Picker
Presets plus a custom color: use Color Picker with its Swatches slot
anatomy: Swatches slot: 6-10 Swatches (Type=color, Size=sm); each Swatch Label is its color name (Blue, Orange, Teal, Amber, Pink, Green, Violet, Rose for chart/1..8)
Selected Swatch: State=selected; the default selects the first, Blue (chart/1)
Label (Show label): the name of the selected color, same as that Swatch's Label
rules: 6-10 colors from the chart palette; one selected
The Label always names the selected swatch; when you select another swatch, change the Label too
Colors come from chart tokens so they stay readable in dark mode
Same order everywhere the palette appears
Show the name under the swatches; never rely on color alone
a11y: A radiogroup with a label ("Label color"); arrow keys move between swatches
Each swatch is labelled with its color name
Items that use the color also show a name or icon
Swatch Picker.code: shadcn RadioGroup of round items (or ToggleGroup type single) with chart token backgrounds.

Form Section.summary: One group of a long form or settings page: title and a sentence on the left, the fields on the right.
use: Settings pages with several groups (billing, contact, security)
Long record forms: a customer, a product, an invoice
Profile pages
avoid: Settings that apply at once, one per row: use Setting Row
A short form of 2-4 fields: use Fields in one column
A group of checkboxes or radios with one label: use Fieldset
rules: Layout: side from 1024 px (heading column 280), stacked on narrow screens and in Sheets
Group fields the way people think about them; 2-6 fields per section
Description says what the fields are for or when changes apply
Divider between sections, off on the last one
One Save for the page, in a Save Bar or Action Bar
a11y: The title is a real heading that follows the page outline
Wrap the section in a section element labelled by its title (aria-labelledby)
Tab order goes from the heading column to the fields, top to bottom
Form Section.code: <section class="grid gap-6 lg:grid-cols-[280px_1fr]"> with h3, p and FormFields; Separator between sections.

Fieldset.summary: A group of related controls with one label: checkboxes, radios, the parts of an address or a date.
use: A checkbox or radio group with a question
The parts of an address or a date
A group of Option Cards
avoid: One control: use Field
A titled group of unrelated fields in a long form: use Form Section
One on/off setting: use Setting Row
anatomy: Options slot: Checkbox, Radio or Fields
rules: State: default, error
The legend names the question ("Notify me about"); the description gives the rule ("Choose at least one.")
The error belongs to the group, not to one control: "Choose at least one notification."
Options in a meaningful order; 2-7 options, more go in a Select or Combobox
a11y: A fieldset with a legend, or role="group" / role="radiogroup" with aria-labelledby
Description and error are linked to the group with aria-describedby
On submit, focus moves to the first control of the group in error
Fieldset.code: <fieldset> with <legend>; shadcn RadioGroup or Checkbox items; FormMessage for the group error.

Error Summary.summary: At the top of a long form after a failed submit: how many fields need a fix and a link to each.
use: Forms longer than one screen
Multi-step forms at the review step
Imports and settings pages with many fields
avoid: Short forms: show inline errors on the Field only
A server or network error: use Alert
A message about a saved action: use Toast
anatomy: Errors slot: one link per field ("Email: enter an email address like name@company.com")
rules: Shows only after a submit; focus moves here
Each link names the field and the fix, the same message the field shows inline
Links in the order of the fields on the page
The count updates as fields are fixed; the summary disappears when all are fixed
a11y: role="alert" or a focused container with tabindex="-1" and a heading
Each link moves focus to its field (href="#field-id")
Error color is paired with the icon and the title text
Error Summary.code: custom: shadcn Alert (destructive) with a list of anchor links built from react-hook-form formState.errors.

Requirement List.summary: Rules checked live while people type or before they publish: password rules, import checks, what a listing needs.
use: Password rules under a new-password field
Checks before a listing or a page goes live
Import checks before people continue
avoid: One strength level for a password: use Password Strength
Errors after a submit: use the Field error or Error Summary
Steps of a process: use Stepper
rules: Each Check Item updates as soon as it is met
Nothing turns red before a submit; pending stays neutral
Under 6 rules, in the order people fix them
Rules are positive and short: "At least 12 characters"
a11y: A list (ul) linked to the field with aria-describedby
Changes are announced politely (aria-live="polite"), not on every key
Met is shown by icon and text, not color alone
Requirement List.code: custom: <ul> of Check Items, state from the zod schema of the field.

Emoji Picker.summary: Searchable grid of emoji for reactions, a status or a workspace icon, opened in a Popover.
use: Picking an emoji for a status or a workspace icon
The + button at the end of a Reaction Bar
Inserting an emoji in a Comment or Chat Composer
avoid: Adding a reaction from a short fixed set: use Reaction Bar
Picking a product icon or a color: use Swatch Picker
Rating or feedback faces: use CSAT Rating
anatomy: Categories: icon tabs (Recent, Smileys, Hearts, Objects, Ideas, World)
rules: Opens in a Popover from a smiley Button Icon; picking an emoji closes it
Recently used first, then categories in a fixed order
Search matches names and keywords ("check", "party"); no results shows "No emoji found"
Skin tone is remembered per person
Enter picks the highlighted emoji; the search keeps focus while arrows move in the grid
a11y: The grid has role="grid" (or listbox) with arrow-key navigation and one tab stop
Each emoji has an accessible name ("thumbs up"), not only the character
Category tabs are buttons with aria-label and aria-pressed for the current one
Escape closes the picker and returns focus to the trigger
Emoji Picker.code: frimousse or emoji-mart in a shadcn Popover; trigger is a ghost Button size="icon".

App Launcher.summary: Grid of the products in a suite, opened from a layout-grid Button Icon in the top bar.
use: Suites with 4 or more apps under one sign-in (Invoices, Payroll, CRM)
Jumping between apps from the Top Bar
Showing which app people are in
avoid: Two or three apps: use Org Switcher or a link in the Top Bar
Switching workspaces or tenants: use Org Switcher
Navigation inside one app: use Sidebar
anatomy: Grid of apps, 3 per row: icon tile and app name
rules: Only for suites with 4 or more apps
App names of one or two words, below the tile, never truncated
Same order for everyone; the current app is highlighted, not moved to the start
Apps the person has no access to are hidden
An app that opens in a new tab shows an external-link icon
a11y: The trigger is a Button Icon with aria-label="Apps" and aria-expanded
Each app is a link; the current one has aria-current="page"
Arrows move in the grid, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger
App Launcher.code: shadcn Popover with a 3-column grid of links (grid-cols-3); trigger is a ghost Button size="icon" with LayoutGrid.

Confirm Popover.summary: A small confirmation next to the button that triggered it, for actions with some cost that do not need a dialog.
use: Archive, remove a person from a project, discard a draft
Row actions in a table where a dialog would hide the context
Bulk actions on a few items ("Archive 3 invoices?")
avoid: Irreversible loss of data: use Alert Dialog
Reversible actions: use a Toast with Undo, no confirmation
A choice with several options or a form: use Dialog
anatomy: Title: a question with the object, ui/label
Description: one line on the consequence, body/small, muted
Actions: Cancel (Button outline sm) and confirm (Button sm, destructive for Tone=destructive)
rules: Title is a question that names the action and the object: "Archive 3 invoices?"
Description says what happens next or how to undo it, in one line
The confirm button repeats the verb ("Archive"); never "OK" or "Yes"
Tone=destructive for remove and discard; default for archive and similar
Opens next to the trigger; clicking outside or Escape cancels
a11y: Focus moves to Cancel when it opens and returns to the trigger when it closes
role="alertdialog" with aria-labelledby on the title and aria-describedby on the description
Escape cancels; Enter on the confirm button runs the action
Confirm Popover.code: shadcn Popover with title, text and two Buttons (PopoverContent role="alertdialog").

Back Link.summary: A link above the page title back to the list the record came from: "All invoices" with a left arrow.
use: Record pages opened from a list (an invoice from All invoices)
Settings subpages that return to the settings overview
Mobile pages without a Breadcrumb
avoid: Hierarchies deeper than two levels: use Breadcrumb
Going back between wizard steps: use the Back button in the Action Bar
Mobile screens with a header: use Mobile Header
anatomy: Label: the destination, ui/label (body/small), muted; foreground on hover
rules: Name the destination ("All invoices"); never "Back"
Return to the list with its filters, sort and scroll position
Sits above the page title, aligned with it; one per page
Links to a fixed URL, so it works when the page is opened from a bookmark
a11y: A real link (<a>), not a button calling history.back()
The arrow icon is aria-hidden; the label says where it goes
Visible focus ring; text meets 4.5:1 in default and hover
Back Link.code: Next.js Link (or <a>) with ArrowLeft, text-sm text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground.

Skip Link.summary: First focusable element of every page, hidden until it gets keyboard focus, that jumps to the main content.
use: Every page and shell: "Skip to main content"
Before a long repeated block, such as a sidebar of 30 links
Pages with a large Navbar or mega menu
avoid: Links between sections of one article: use Table of Contents
Going back to the top of a long page: use Button Icon
Links people see and use all the time: use Nav Link or the Sidebar
anatomy: Label: "Skip to main content" (or "Skip to results" before a long filter block), on a surface with border and shadow, top left
rules: The first element in the tab order of every page
Hidden until focused, then shown top left above everything
Moves focus to the main content (the <main> landmark or the page title)
Add one per long repeated block; never remove it
a11y: A link to #main; the target has tabindex="-1" so it can take focus
Visible focus style with at least 3:1 against the page
Use sr-only with focus:not-sr-only; never display:none
Skip Link.code: <a href="#main" class="sr-only focus:not-sr-only focus:fixed focus:left-4 focus:top-4 focus:z-50">.

Page Toolbar.summary: The row between a list page title and the list: search and Filters on the left, Toggle Group and the primary action on the right.
use: List pages: invoices, customers, orders
Pages that switch between table, board and calendar views
Lists with a few filters behind one Filters button
avoid: Rows are selected: use Table Toolbar
Data grids with saved views, columns and density: use Data Grid Toolbar
Several filters always visible as chips: use Filter Bar
anatomy: Filters: Button outline with Icon/list-filter (Show filters)
Filter count: Badge Count with the number of active filters
rules: One primary action, on the right ("New invoice")
The filter count shows only when filters are on
Search, filters and view live in the URL
While rows are selected, Table Toolbar takes its place
On narrow screens search takes the full row and the rest wraps below
a11y: Search has an aria-label that says what it searches
The Filters button includes the count in its name: "Filters, 2 active"
Tab order: search, filters, view, primary
Page Toolbar.code: custom: flex justify-between with shadcn Input, Button + Badge, ToggleGroup and Button.

Account Menu.summary: The menu behind the signed-in person's avatar: name and email, personal settings, and Log out.
use: Avatar in the Top Bar
Sidebar User at the bottom of the Sidebar
Personal items: Profile, Settings, Theme, Keyboard shortcuts
avoid: Switching workspace or company: use Org Switcher
Actions on a record: use Menu
Product navigation: use Sidebar
anatomy: Header: Avatar, name (ui/label) and email (body/small, muted)
Menu Items: Profile, Settings, Theme, Keyboard shortcuts
rules: Personal items only; workspace items go in Org Switcher
Log out is last, after a Separator
Log out never asks for confirmation unless there are unsaved changes
Long emails truncate with an ellipsis and show in full in a Tooltip
Theme opens a submenu (Light, Dark, System) with a check on the current one
a11y: The trigger has aria-label="Account menu" (or the person's name) and aria-haspopup="menu"
Arrows move, Enter selects, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger
The header is not focusable; it is read as the menu label
Account Menu.code: shadcn DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuLabel (Avatar, name, email), DropdownMenuItems and DropdownMenuSeparator.

Notification Item.summary: One notification: who did what to which object, when and where, with an unread dot and optional actions.
use: Rows in the Notification Center
The full notifications page
Approvals, mentions and assignments people can act on from the list
avoid: Result of the person's own action: use Toast
Changes on one record over time: use Timeline Item
A message that blocks the page: use Alert
anatomy: Message: "Elena Popa approved INV-1041 for €2,450.00", actor and object in bold
Meta: time and area, body/small, muted
Actions slot (Show actions): one or two Buttons sm
rules: Message names the actor, the action and the object; two lines at most
State=unread has a muted background and the dot
The whole row opens the object and marks it read
Actions only for what people can do from the list (Approve, View invoice); at most two
System notifications without a person use an icon Avatar
a11y: The row is a link; actions are separate buttons, not nested in the link
Unread is in the accessible name ("Unread: Elena Popa approved..."), not color or the dot alone
The time is a <time> element with the full date in a title
Notification Item.code: custom row: shadcn Avatar, text and Buttons; unread dot as a span with sr-only text.

Notification Center.summary: The panel behind the bell in the top bar: latest notifications by type, newest first, with Mark all as read and View all.
use: The bell in the Top Bar
Products with mentions, approvals and assignments
Quick triage without leaving the page
avoid: The full history with filters: use Block / Notifications
Choosing channels and frequency: use Block / Notification Preferences
Feedback on the person's own action: use Toast
anatomy: Header: title and Mark all as read (Button ghost sm)
rules: Newest first, unread on top; 5-8 items, then View all
The bell shows a Badge Count of unread items
Opening the panel does not mark items read; opening an item does
Empty: "You are all caught up."
Mark all as read applies to the current tab
Show tabs only when there are several kinds of notification; one kind needs no tabs
a11y: The bell is a button with the count in its name: "Notifications, 3 unread"
New items are announced with aria-live="polite" on the count, never by moving focus
Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the bell
Notification Center.code: shadcn Popover with Tabs and a ScrollArea of Notification Items; trigger Button size="icon" + Badge.

Search Result Item.summary: One result on a search page, 640 wide. Type says what was found: page, record, person, file, media, product, event or a featured answer; each shows the parts people need to pick the right result.
use: Search results pages for help centers and docs (Type=page)
Global search across the app: records, people and files in one list or in tabs
Search on content and shop sites: videos (media), products, events
One featured or AI answer above the results (Type=answer)
avoid: Suggestions while typing: use Command Dialog
A list of records to manage: use a table of Table Cells or List Items
Product grids and catalog listings: use Product Card
Agenda or event listings: use Event Card
Related links under an article: use Post Card
anatomy: Type=page: Path (Show path): Path, Icon/chevron-right, Section; Title (body/large, 2 lines); Snippet (body/small, 2 lines, matched words bold); meta (Show meta): type Badge and Updated
Type=record: icon tile (Icon swap, 40, background/muted); Record (title, 2 lines) with a status Badge (exposed); Record details (Show meta): "Invoice · €1,240.00 · Due 30 Oct 2026 · Updated 12 Oct"
Type=person: Avatar lg (exposed: Initials or photo); Name; Role (role and team, 2 lines); Email (Show meta); action (Show action): outline Button sm "Message" (exposed)

Type=file: icon tile (Icon swap: file type); File name; meta (Show meta): File details ("PDF · 2.4 MB · Updated 12 Oct"), owner Avatar xs (exposed) and Owner; download (Show action): ghost Button Icon
Type=media: Video Thumbnail 160 x 90 with duration (exposed); Media title; Media summary (2 lines); Media details (Show meta): "Video · Acme Academy · Updated 12 Oct 2026"
Type=product: Image Placeholder 1:1, 80; Product; Price sm (exposed); Rating sm with count (exposed, Show meta); Product summary (2 lines)
Type=event: Date Tile (exposed); Event with a format Badge (exposed, "Webinar"); When and where (Show meta): date, time with time zone, place

Type=answer: muted card (background/muted, radius/lg, spacing/4); label: AI Notice label (exposed, "AI answer", or a Badge "Best answer"); Question; Answer (body/default, 4 lines); Sources slot (Source Items or Citations); feedback (Show feedback): "Was this helpful?" and thumbs up / down
Each type has its own text properties; Title, Snippet, Path, Section and Updated belong to page only. Show meta, Show action and Icon are shared
rules: One Type per result: pick the one that matches what opens on click
Pick the Type before typing text: text properties are per type, so text does not carry over when you switch
Group results by type with a heading per group, or tab by type (All, Pages, People, Files with counts); inside a tab use one Type
At most one answer, always first, and only when it is grounded in sources people can open
Never mix widths or densities in one list; keep the same Show path and Show meta choice for every row of a group
Titles wrap to 2 lines, snippets and summaries to 2 (Answer to 4), then ellipsis; bold the matched terms
Records show their status Badge; files show format and size before people click; people show role and team
No results: Empty State that repeats the query and suggests other words
a11y: Results are a list; each title is a link and a heading; the leading visual is decorative (alt="") unless it adds information
Matched terms use <mark> (or strong), with contrast that does not rely on color alone
The result count is announced in a live region when the query or tab changes
Row actions (Message, download, feedback) are separate buttons whose labels name the result ("Download Q3 revenue report, PDF, 2.4 MB")
The answer is a region labeled "AI answer" with its sources as links
Search Result Item.code:
custom:
  • per result with a type switch; page = breadcrumb, heading,

    , Badge; leading Avatar, Badge, Button, Price, Rating from the system; answer = Card (muted) with sources as links.

Show More.summary: A long text cut to 3 lines with a Show more / Show less toggle.
use: Notes, descriptions and bios on a record page
Long reviews or comments in a list
Product or job descriptions where the start says enough
avoid: Several sections to open: use Accordion
A whole article or long rich content: use Sheet or a page of its own
Long lists of items: use Load More
anatomy: Text: body/default, 3 lines when collapsed, fade or ellipsis at the cut
rules: Only when the full text is rarely needed; key information stays above the cut
Show the toggle only when the text is longer than 3 lines
Show less returns to the same scroll position
Never cut in the middle of a word
a11y: The toggle is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls on the text
Focus stays on the toggle; the expanded text is announced
The full text is in the DOM, cut with line-clamp, so screen readers can reach it
Show More.code:
shadcn Collapsible, or a

toggled by a Button variant="link".

Load More.summary: End of a feed or a long list that grows in place: how many are shown out of the total, and a button for the next page.
use: Feeds and activity
Search results browsed once
Lists of cards, comments or reviews
avoid: Tables where people jump to a page: use Pagination
Tables with rows per page: use Table Pagination
Narrow lists inside a card: use Pagination Compact
anatomy: Button (exposed instance): Label "Load 20 more", outline (State=loading shows a Spinner)
rules: The label says how many it loads ("Load 20 more")
Hide the button when everything is shown; keep the count
Keep the scroll position and move focus to the first new item
Loading keeps the button width and disables it
On error, keep the loaded items and show Retry
a11y: The count is in a live region (aria-live="polite") and updates after loading
The button has aria-busy while loading
Focus moves to the first new item so keyboard users continue from there
Load More.code: shadcn Button variant="outline" with a count; TanStack Query useInfiniteQuery (fetchNextPage).

Shortcut Row.summary: One keyboard shortcut in the shortcuts dialog or a help page: what it does, then the keys.
use: The keyboard shortcuts dialog opened with ?
Help and docs pages that list shortcuts
Keyboard shortcuts from the Account Menu
avoid: A shortcut next to a menu label: use Menu Item with Shortcut
A shortcut hint on a button: use Tooltip with Kbd
Keys inline in prose: use Kbd or Kbd Group
rules: Action is a verb phrase in sentence case: "Open command menu"
Group rows by area (Navigation, Editing) with a heading per group
Show ⌘ on Mac and Ctrl on Windows and Linux
Key sequences (G then I) read as separate keys with "then" between them
List only shortcuts that work
a11y: Rows are a description list (dt action, dd keys) or a table
Keys use <kbd> with readable names for symbols ("Command K")
Text meets 4.5:1 on the row background
Shortcut Row.code: custom: <div class="flex justify-between"> with text and shadcn Kbd / KbdGroup.

Resizable Panels.summary: Two panels with a handle to drag the split: list and detail, editor and preview, code and output.
use: List and detail side by side (inbox, tickets)
Editor and preview
Code and output, or a query and its results
avoid: A detail that opens on demand over the list: use Sheet
A fixed panel of properties next to an editor: use Side Panel
Small screens: use a Sheet for the detail over the list
rules: Each panel has a minimum width; content never squeezes below it
Double-click the handle to reset the split
The split is remembered per person
On narrow screens show one panel at a time with a way back
A panel can collapse to a rail when dragged past its minimum
a11y: The handle has role="separator" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax
Focus the handle and use arrows to resize; Enter collapses or restores
The handle has a visible focus ring and a 3:1 contrast against the panels
Resizable Panels.code: shadcn Resizable (react-resizable-panels) with autoSaveId to remember the split.

FAB.summary: Floating action button for the one main action on a mobile screen: new invoice, compose, add.
use: The main create action on a mobile list (New invoice)
Compose in a mobile inbox or feed
Type=extended on a first visit or empty lists, shrinking to the icon on scroll
avoid: Desktop: use a primary Button in the Page Header
Destructive or secondary actions: use Action Sheet or Menu
Several actions: use Action Sheet
rules: One per screen, for the main action only
Bottom right, 16 px from the edges, above the Bottom Nav
Extended shows a label and shrinks to the icon on scroll
Never covers the last row of content; add bottom padding to the list
Hidden while the keyboard is open
a11y: Icon only: aria-label with the action ("New invoice")
Touch target at least 48 by 48 px
Placed in the DOM after the main content, before the Bottom Nav, so the tab order follows the screen
FAB.code: shadcn Button size="icon" rounded-full shadow-lg, fixed bottom-20 right-4 (bottom-4 without Bottom Nav).

Action Sheet.summary: A short list of actions for one item on mobile, rising from the bottom, with Cancel apart.
use: Actions on one item on mobile: share, duplicate, download, delete
The More button on a mobile record page
A long press on a row in a mobile list
avoid: Content or a form: use Drawer
Desktop: use Menu
One main action: use FAB or a Button
anatomy: Header (Show header): Title (the object) and Description
Actions: Action 1, Action 2, Action 3, each with an icon swap (Action 1 icon ...), one per row
Destructive action (+ Destructive action icon): last, in red
rules: 2-6 actions, one line each, verbs
Destructive last and red; it still asks for confirmation when it cannot be undone
Cancel sits apart at the bottom
Tap outside or swipe down closes it
Title names the object ("INV-2041")
a11y: role="menu" with menuitem rows, or a list of buttons in a dialog; focus moves to the first action
Escape and Cancel close it and return focus to the trigger
Rows are at least 48 px high; destructive is named by its label, not color alone
Action Sheet.code: shadcn Drawer (vaul) with a list of Buttons and a separate Cancel; desktop falls back to DropdownMenu.

Annotation Pin.summary: A numbered marker on a design, document or screenshot where a comment lives.
use: Comments on a design, a PDF or a screenshot
Review feedback tied to a spot on an image
Numbered callouts that match a comment list
avoid: Pointing out a feature in the product: use Hotspot
A tour step: use Coachmark
Comments on a whole record: use Comment
anatomy: Pin: round with the point at the bottom-left corner
Number: the comment's position in the list
rules: The point (bottom-left corner) marks the spot
Numbers match the comment list order
Click opens the thread in a Popover or the side panel; State=active is the open one
Resolved pins fade and show a check
Pins that overlap move apart and stay clickable
a11y: Each pin is a button: "Comment 3 by Elena Popa"
Tab order follows the numbers; Enter opens the thread
Pins are also reachable from the comment list, which is the main way for screen readers
Annotation Pin.code: custom: absolutely positioned Button (percent coordinates) + shadcn Popover for the thread.

Social Share.summary: Share buttons for a public page: copy link, email, the system share sheet and up to three networks.
use: Articles, blog posts and changelog entries
Public event, job or product pages
The end of a public report or case study
avoid: Sharing a record with people in the workspace: use Share Link Row
A link people copy and paste: use Copy Field
Inviting teammates: use Invite Row
anatomy: Networks (Show networks): up to three network marks
rules: Copy link first; it confirms with a Toast ("Link copied")
Up to three networks the audience uses
Replace the letter marks with the networks' official logos in product
The system share button shows only where the browser supports it
Shared links open with a title, description and image (Open Graph)
a11y: Each button has an aria-label: "Copy link", "Share by email", "Share on LinkedIn"
Network links that open a new window say so ("opens in a new tab")
Icons meet 3:1 against the background
Social Share.code: shadcn Button size="icon" variant="outline"; navigator.clipboard, mailto:, navigator.share and network share URLs.

Trend Indicator.summary: A change against a period: arrow, signed percent or amount, and what it is compared to. Trend says which way it moved; Tone says if that is good, bad or neither.
use: The change under a value in a Metric Strip or a Stat Card
A change next to a figure in a table row or a report header
Rising costs or churn: Trend=up with Tone=negative
Style=badge inside KPI tiles and table cells, where a pill reads better than colored text
avoid: A trend people read over time: use Sparkline or Line Chart
A value against a target: use Bullet Chart or Progress Card
A status with no change: use Badge
anatomy: Style: text (colored icon and value) or badge (icon and value in a soft Badge: soft-success, soft-destructive, soft-neutral by Tone)
Icon: trending-up, trending-down or minus (from Trend)
Value: signed percent or amount, ui/label (Style=badge: the Badge Label, edited on the exposed Badge)
Comparison (Show comparison): "vs last month", ui/caption, muted
rules: Trend follows the data; Tone follows the meaning (costs up is negative, churn down is positive)
Always signed: +12.4%, −3.1%, 0.0% for flat; one decimal for percentages
The comparison names the period ("vs last month", "vs Q3"); hide it only when the period is said once nearby
Edit the value text per instance; keep the same comparison for every item in a row
Neutral tone when the change is too small to matter, or when up and down mean nothing good or bad
One Style per row of metrics
a11y: The sign and the words carry the meaning; color only supports it
The icon is decorative (aria-hidden); read as "Up 12.4% vs last month" with a visually hidden "Up" or "Down"
Positive and negative text keeps 4.5:1 on card and page in every mode
Trend Indicator.code: custom: lucide TrendingUp, TrendingDown or Minus + <span class="tabular-nums">; tone as text-success, text-destructive or text-muted-foreground. Style=badge: shadcn Badge soft variant with the icon inside.

Metric Strip Item.summary: One figure in a Metric Strip: label, value and an optional Trend Indicator.
use: Each figure of a Metric Strip
avoid: A figure on its own with a footnote or chart: use Stat Card
A number with no trend outside a strip: use Figure
rules: Show divider off on the first item, on for every item after it
Value stays on one line; amounts in the locale format and compact (€1.84M)
Label is a noun of one to three words, sentence case
Show trend on all items in a strip or on none
a11y: Label and value are read together (dt and dd)
The divider is decorative
Metric Strip Item.code: custom: <div> with <dt>, <dd class="tabular-nums"> and Trend Indicator; divider as border-l.

Metric Strip.summary: A row of 3-5 key figures at the top of a dashboard, report or record page, lighter than Stat Cards: label, value, trend, dividers between.
use: Key figures above a report or dashboard: revenue, invoices, overdue, days to pay
The summary at the top of a record page (customer totals)
A dense header where a row of Stat Cards would take too much space
avoid: Figures that need a footnote or a chart each: use Stat Card
One figure against a target: use Progress Card or Gauge
Counts in a page header with no trend: use Figure
anatomy: Metrics slot: 3-5 Metric Strip Items, Show divider on after the first
rules: 3-5 figures; more go in a table or a second section
Same period for every item, said once nearby ("Last 30 days" in the header)
Most important figure first, in the same order on every visit
Items share the width equally; on narrow screens wrap to two columns, no horizontal scroll
Loading: Skeleton in each value; no data: "No data" in muted text, never 0
a11y: Code as a <dl> with one dt and dd per figure
The period is in text near the strip, so each figure is read with it
Trend reads as text ("Up 12% vs last month")
Metric Strip.code: custom: <dl class="grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 divide-x"> of Metric Strip Items.

Usage Meter.summary: How much of a plan limit is used: seats, storage, API calls, documents per month. Label, used of limit, bar and a hint.
use: Billing and plan settings: one meter per limit
Next to the action that uses the limit (invite a member, upload a file)
Team Members header: seats used
avoid: A goal people try to reach: use Progress Card
Progress of a running task: use Progress
Parts of one total: use Distribution Bar
anatomy: Hint (Show hint): what to do, or the consequence and the date
rules: Level=near from 80%: warning tone and say what to do ("Upgrade or remove members")
Level=over above 100%: error tone, say the consequence and the date ("Uploads pause on 1 Nov")
Usage shows used and limit with the unit ("4.2 of 5 GB"); unlimited plans show the count and no bar
Say when the count resets for monthly limits ("Resets 1 Nov")
Offer the fix in the hint or next to it: Upgrade, Buy more, Manage
a11y: The bar has role="meter" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemax and a label ("Seats used")
Level is in the hint text, never color alone
Crossing near or over is announced once in a polite live region, not on every render
Usage Meter.code: shadcn Progress with a tone class + label row; role="meter" and aria-value* on the bar.

Countdown.summary: Time left until a deadline people act on: an offer, a webinar start, a payment due, a session that expires.
use: A real deadline: offer ends, registration closes, webinar starts
A payment due or a session that expires
A resend code timer (short form, minutes and seconds)
avoid: Fake urgency that resets: use Meta Item with the real date, or nothing
A date far ahead (more than 30 days): use the date with Meta Item
Progress of a running job: use Progress
rules: Days, hours, minutes; seconds only in the last hour (Show seconds)
Always say what happens at zero next to it, with the exact date and time zone ("Offer ends 24 Oct, 18:00 CEST")
Two digits per tile (02, 14); drop the days tile when it is 00
At zero, replace it with the outcome ("Registration closed") and remove the action it promoted
Count from the server time, never only the device clock
a11y: Screen readers get the end time, not a ticking value: role="timer" with aria-live="off" and a <time datetime> label
Announce once at a meaningful step (5 minutes left) for session expiry, with a way to extend
No flashing or color pulse in the last seconds
Countdown.code: custom: tiles from a useCountdown hook (setInterval 1 s, server end time); <time datetime> for the deadline.

Leaderboard Row.summary: A ranked person or team: rank, avatar, name and value.
use: Sales targets: top account managers this quarter
Support resolution or contributions per team
The viewer's own row under the top 10 (State=current)
avoid: Public rankings that shame people: show the viewer their own progress with Progress Card
Ranking categories or products: use Bar Chart Horizontal
A plain list of people: use List Item or Byline
anatomy: Value: tabular, right-aligned, with the unit
State=current: highlighted row for the viewer
rules: Top 5-10, then the viewer's row (State=current) when they are below, with a gap marker between
Value says the unit (€48,250, 312 tickets); same unit for every row
Ties share a rank (1, 2, 2, 4)
Say the period and the measure above the list ("Paid revenue, Q4")
Long names truncate with a Tooltip; value never truncates
a11y: Code as an <ol> or a table with rank, name and value columns
The current row has aria-current="true" and a visible "You" label, not only a tint
The Avatar is decorative next to the name (alt="")
Leaderboard Row.code: custom: <ol> of rows, shadcn Avatar, tabular-nums value; current row bg-accent.

Command Snippet.summary: One command or value people copy into a terminal or config: install line, CLI command, environment variable.
use: Install steps in docs and onboarding (npm install @acme/sdk)
A CLI command or one environment variable
A value to paste into another tool: webhook URL, key id
avoid: Several lines or command output: use Code Block
A secret key shown once: use the API Keys block with a masked value and Copy
Code inside a sentence: inline code style
anatomy: Command: mono on background/muted, one line
Copy: Button Icon ghost sm (check for 2 s)
rules: One command per snippet; never include the $ in what gets copied
Long commands scroll horizontally, never wrap
Copy shows a check for 2 s, then returns to the copy icon
Show prompt off for values that are not terminal commands (URLs, env values)
Placeholders the user must replace are named in caps (YOUR_API_KEY) and explained below
a11y: Copy is labelled "Copy command"; "Copied" is announced politely (aria-live)
The prompt is aria-hidden and excluded from selection (select-none)
Mono text keeps 4.5:1 on background/muted
Command Snippet.code: custom: <pre><code> on bg-muted + shadcn Button size="icon" with navigator.clipboard.writeText.

Endpoint Row.summary: One API endpoint in a reference list: method badge, path in mono with parameters in braces, and a one-line summary.
use: API reference sidebar or overview lists
The endpoints a webhook or integration uses
Grouped lists per resource: Invoices, Customers
avoid: The full request and response: use Code Block or JSON Viewer
A navigation item with no method: use Nav Link
One command to copy: use Command Snippet
anatomy: Method: Badge (GET info, POST success, PUT and PATCH warning, DELETE destructive)
State: default, hover (background/muted), selected (background/accent) for the open endpoint
rules: Methods keep the same color everywhere; the method name is always written
Path in mono, parameters in braces, no host
Summary starts with a verb: "Retrieve an invoice"
The whole row links to the endpoint page; the open endpoint is State=selected, one per list
Order within a resource: list, create, retrieve, update, delete
a11y: The row is one link with an accessible name of method, path and summary
Method is text in the Badge, never color alone
Paths do not break mid-segment; long paths wrap at slashes
The selected row has aria-current="page"
Endpoint Row.code: custom: <a> row with shadcn Badge (method variant) + <code> path + summary.

Log Row.summary: One line of a log or event stream: time with milliseconds, level and message in mono.
use: Live tails of request, job or deploy logs
Search results in a log viewer
Webhook delivery and integration event history
avoid: Who changed what on a record: use the Audit Log with Change Item
Events people read as a story: use Timeline Item
A structured payload: use JSON Viewer in the expanded row
rules: Newest at the bottom in live tails, at the top in searches
Long messages wrap, never truncate
Level filter and search above the list; pause the tail while the user scrolls up
Time zone stated once in the header; times in the same zone
Rows expand to show the payload (JSON Viewer) and the request id
a11y: Code as a list or a log region (role="log", aria-live="polite" only for live tails, paused on demand)
Level is text, never color alone
The rows are keyboard focusable when they expand
Log Row.code: custom: virtualized list (@tanstack/react-virtual) of mono rows; level as a text label.

Diff Line.summary: One line of a diff: number, marker, sign and text. Part of Diff Viewer.
use: Each line of a Diff Viewer
avoid: One field that changed on a record: use Change Item
anatomy: Marker: color strip (added success, removed destructive)
Text: added, removed with strikethrough, or context
rules: Type=added in success, Type=removed in destructive with strikethrough, context plain
The sign is always shown for added and removed lines
Removed lines come above the added lines that replace them
Text keeps its whitespace; long lines wrap in prose and scroll in code
a11y: The sign carries the meaning; screen readers get "added" or "removed" as visually hidden text
Line numbers are aria-hidden
Diff Line.code: custom: row in a <table> or grid; diff from jsdiff (diffLines).

Diff Viewer.summary: What changed between two versions of a text, contract, config or code: file name with counts, then Diff Lines.
use: Preview of a version in a version history (Version Item, State=selected)
Changes to a contract, template or terms before approval
Config or code changes in a deploy or review
avoid: Field-level changes of a record: use Change Item
A single code example: use Code Block
Release notes for users: use Release Note Item
anatomy: Header: file-text icon, file name, added count, removed count
rules: Show 3 lines of context around each change and collapse the rest ("Show 24 unchanged lines")
Removed lines above added lines
Counts in the header: +3 −1
Unified by default; side by side only on wide screens (1024 and up)
No changes: say "No differences" instead of an empty frame
a11y: Each line names its type in hidden text (added, removed), so color is not the only cue
Collapsed sections are buttons with the count in their label
The header counts are text, read as "3 added, 1 removed"
Diff Viewer.code: custom on jsdiff (diffLines); react-diff-viewer-continued for side by side.

JSON Viewer.summary: Structured data people inspect: webhook payloads, API responses, event properties, audit details. Objects and arrays collapse. The copy action sits in the surrounding header (Card Header or panel), not in the viewer.
use: Webhook payloads and API responses in a log or delivery detail
Event properties in analytics or audit details
Metadata of a record in an admin view
avoid: A short example people copy: use Code Block
Editing data: use a form, or a code editor (Monaco, CodeMirror)
Field changes: use Change Item
anatomy: Lines: chevron for objects and arrays, then key and value in mono (code) on background/muted
Values: strings chart/3, numbers chart/1, booleans in a chart color; keys and punctuation foreground/default
No header and no TEXT properties: the content is pasted per instance, one text node per line
rules: To edit: change a line's text, then reapply the value color to the value only (keys stay foreground/default); add or remove line frames for longer or shorter payloads
Put the title and Copy in the surrounding header (Card Header action or panel header), not in the viewer
Large payloads open collapsed after the first level; collapsed nodes show a count ("items: [3]")
Copy copies the whole payload, formatted
Long strings wrap; null shows as null, never blank
Mask secrets (tokens, card numbers) before they reach the viewer
a11y: Code as a tree (role="tree", role="treeitem", aria-expanded); arrow keys open and close nodes
Value types are readable without color: quotes for strings
Value colors keep 4.5:1 on background/muted
JSON Viewer.code: custom tree on <pre>, or react-json-view-lite themed with tokens; Copy with navigator.clipboard.

Dashboard Widget.summary: A movable, resizable tile on a customizable dashboard: drag handle, title, period, refresh, expand and menu, any chart or KPI in Content.
use: Dashboards people arrange themselves
Home pages with a chosen set of KPIs and charts
Saved dashboards shared with a team
avoid: A fixed report: use Chart Card
One number on a fixed page: use Stat Card
Figures in one row: use Metric Strip
anatomy: Refresh, Expand and More: Button Icon ghost sm
Content slot: fills the widget width and hugs its content height; a chart, a Sparkline, a KPI or a list
rules: Snap to a 12-column grid; sizes 3, 4, 6 or 12 columns
Edit mode shows the handles and resize corner; view mode hides them
Period is written on every widget; a dashboard-wide period says so once
Menu: edit, duplicate, change size, remove (with Undo)
Each widget loads, fails and refreshes on its own: Skeleton, inline Alert with Retry, never a blank tile
Widgets in one row share a height: the tallest hugs, the others fill the row so footers line up
a11y: Moving and resizing work by keyboard: menu items "Move left", "Move right", "Change size"; the new place is announced
Icon buttons have labels ("Refresh Invoices paid")
The widget is a region named by its title
Dashboard Widget.code: react-grid-layout (12 cols) with shadcn Card per item; drag handle via draggableHandle.

Distribution Bar.summary: Parts of one whole as a single 100% bar: invoices by status, budget by category, storage by type.
use: Invoices by status with a total
Budget or spend by category
Storage by file type in billing settings
avoid: More than 6 parts or comparing groups: use stacked Bar Chart
Part of a whole as the main visual of a card: use Donut Chart
Usage of a limit: use Usage Meter
rules: 2-6 segments in a fixed order, largest or most important first; the rest in "Other"
Segment colors follow the entity (chart/1..6) and stay the same across pages
Legend shows the share (42%); hover a segment for the count
2 px gap between segments; tiny segments keep a 4 px minimum width
Shares add to 100%; round the largest to fix rounding
a11y: The legend carries label and share in text, so color is not the only cue
Segments are focusable with a Tooltip that has the count; or the bar is aria-hidden and the legend is a list
Adjacent segments keep 3:1 against each other or the gap separates them
Distribution Bar.code: custom: flex row of segments with width from the share + legend <ul>; or Recharts BarChart layout="vertical" stacked to 100%.

Bullet Chart.summary: One measure against its target and bands (poor, fair, good) in one line: revenue vs plan, SLA vs goal.
use: Revenue vs plan, SLA vs goal
A stack of KPIs on the same scale for a review
Tables and dense dashboards where a Gauge is too large
avoid: A single percent toward a goal: use Progress or Gauge
Trend over time: use Line Chart
Many items compared to each other: use Bar Chart Horizontal
anatomy: Label: Title and Unit ("EUR, this quarter")
rules: The dark bar is the actual, the line the target, the grey bands the ranges
Bands are named in the legend or footnote (poor, fair, good) with their limits
Stacked bullets share the same scale when the units match
Scale starts at 0; values written as text next to the track (412k, target 480k)
Unit and period in the label
a11y: Actual and target are text, so the line and bar are not the only cue
In code use role="meter" with aria-valuenow and a label that includes the target
Value bar keeps 3:1 against the bands
Bullet Chart.code: custom SVG or Recharts BarChart layout="vertical" with stacked range bars, a thin value Bar and a ReferenceLine for the target.

Radar Chart.summary: Compares 1-3 items across 5-8 qualities on the same scale: vendor scores, skill profiles, plan features.
use: Vendor or tender scores across criteria
Skill or competency profiles
Comparing two plans on qualities with the same scale
avoid: More than 3 series or precise values: use grouped Bar Chart or a table
Change over time: use Line Chart
Qualities on different scales: use a table
anatomy: Series areas and lines: chart/1, chart/2, chart/3
rules: 5-8 axes; same scale on every axis, starting at the center
1-3 series; area fill low opacity so overlaps stay readable
Labels outside the grid, short (one or two words)
Axis order stays fixed and groups related qualities
Legend for 2+ series; tooltip lists every axis value of the hovered series
a11y: Every Radar Chart has a table view with each quality and score
Series differ by line style or markers too, not color alone
Lines and labels keep 3:1 on card and page in every mode
Radar Chart.code: shadcn Chart (Recharts) RadarChart with PolarGrid, PolarAngleAxis and Radar per series; var(--chart-N).

Sankey Chart.summary: How amounts flow from sources to outcomes: payment method to paid or overdue, traffic source to sign-up, budget to spend.
use: Payment method to paid or overdue
Traffic source to sign-up and plan
Budget lines to spend by department
avoid: Drop-off between ordered steps: use Funnel Chart
Parts of one total: use Distribution Bar or Donut Chart
A start total changed by steps: use Waterfall Chart
anatomy: Source nodes (left): fixed 12 wide, pinned left, heights scale
Flows: band width is the amount, colored by source; stretch with the width, scale with the height
Outcome nodes (right): fixed 12 wide, pinned right
Node labels with values, centered on their node
rules: Resize the instance (or set it to Fill in a Chart Card) instead of redrawing; keep at least 480 x 210
2-3 columns and under 12 nodes; fold small flows into "Other"
Label every node with its value (Card €184K)
Color bands by source with chart/1..8; nodes in neutral
Order nodes so bands cross as little as possible
Hover a band for the exact amount and its share of the source
a11y: The table view lists each flow: source, target, amount
Labels are text on the node, not only in a tooltip
Bands keep enough contrast on card (low opacity fills, darker on hover)
Sankey Chart.code: shadcn Chart (Recharts) Sankey with custom node and link renderers; colors via var(--chart-N).

Choropleth Map.summary: Values by region on a map, shaded from light (low) to dark (high): revenue by county, customers by country.
use: Revenue or customers by country, county or region
Where place matters to the decision (sales territories, shipping zones)
A tile layout when equal-size regions read better than real shapes
avoid: Ranking regions precisely: use Bar Chart Horizontal
An address or office location: use Map
Two dimensions that are not places: use Heatmap
anatomy: Regions: shade and code (tile layout, or real map shapes)
rules: One measure, one hue, 5 steps; muted for no data, said in the legend
Replace the tile regions with real map shapes, or keep tiles when equal size reads better
Normalize when size skews the map (per customer, per capita)
Legend states the unit and the step limits
Hover a region for its name and value
a11y: The table view lists every region with its value
Regions are focusable with name and value in the label; or the map is aria-hidden next to the table
Darkest and lightest steps keep 3:1 against the surface; borders separate neighbors
Choropleth Map.code: react-simple-maps with a d3-scale quantize scale on one chart hue; tile grid as a CSS grid of cells.

Version Item.summary: One saved version in a version history panel: who, when, what changed, and Restore.
use: Version history of a document, template or contract
History of a configuration (workflow, price list)
A Side Panel next to the editor with the versions newest first
avoid: Field-level changes of a record: use Change Item
Events by many people on a record: use Timeline Item
Product release notes: use Release Note Item
rules: Newest first; the current version is marked and has no Restore
Selecting a version previews it (State=selected) with a Diff Viewer
Restoring creates a new version; it never deletes the newer ones
Summary says what changed in one line; autosaved versions say "Autosave"
Group autosaves by session or day when there are many
a11y: The list is a listbox or a list of buttons; the selected one has aria-selected or aria-current
Restore is a labelled button ("Restore version from 12 Oct, 15:40")
Dates in a <time> element
Version Item.code: custom: list of rows with shadcn Avatar, Badge and Button; preview via Diff Viewer.

Release Note Item.summary: One entry of a changelog or What's new: type badge, version and date, a title that says the benefit, two sentences on how to use it, optional screenshot, tagged change lines and link.
use: Public changelog pages
In-app What's new: the last 3-5 entries with a link to the full changelog
Release notes in a help center
A release with several changes: Show changes with one Release Note Line per change (Block / Changelog)
avoid: Version history of a document: use Version Item
A system notice people must act on: use Alert
A one-off product tip: use Coachmark
anatomy: Type: Badge (New info, Improved secondary, Fixed success)
Text (Show text): two sentences on how to use it; off when the change lines say it all
Changes (Show changes): slot with Release Note Line instances (Type=new, improved, fixed and Text)
rules: Newest first; one entry per release or per change
Title says the benefit for the user, not the feature name
Text: two sentences: what changed and where to find it (Settings → Reminders)
Type from the variant: new, improved, fixed; for a release with lines, the type of the headline change
Changes: 2-5 lines, New first, then Improved, then Fixed; one sentence each
Screenshot only when it shows where to click; link to the help article
a11y: Each entry is an <article> with the title as a heading

To-dos of a project or a record
Steps before a close or a launch
avoid: Steps people must do in order: use Stepper
A choice in a form: use Checkbox
Cards on a board: use Kanban Card
anatomy: Due (Show due): ui/caption, muted; destructive when overdue
Action slot (Show action): one Button, such as Connect or Start
rules: Ticking saves at once and can be undone (toast with Undo)
Done is struck through and moves to the end
Overdue says it in destructive ("Overdue · 12 Oct")
Open items sort by due date; the title wraps to two lines at most
The row opens the task; the Checkbox only ticks; the action button starts the task
a11y: The Checkbox is labelled by the title
Overdue and done are in text, not color or strikethrough alone
The assignee Avatar has the person's name as alt
Task Item.code: custom row: shadcn Checkbox and Avatar; optimistic update with an Undo toast (Sonner).

Range Input.summary: Two fields for a minimum and a maximum: price or amount filters, typed date ranges, quantities.
use: Price or amount filters in a Filter Section
Quantities and sizes with a lower and an upper bound
Ranges people type, next to a Slider Type=range
avoid: A range people scan visually: use Slider Type=range with these fields next to it
A date range with a calendar: use Date Range Picker
One value: use Input Group or Number Input
rules: State: default, error
Either side may stay empty ("from 100")
Error when min is above max; say it once under the pair: "Minimum must be lower than the maximum"
Same unit and format on both sides; format on blur
In filters, apply on blur or Enter, not on every key
a11y: Wrap the pair in a fieldset or group with the label ("Price")
Each input has its own label: "Minimum price", "Maximum price"
The error is linked to both inputs with aria-describedby
Range Input.code: custom: two shadcn InputGroups in a fieldset; zod refine for min <= max.

Prompt Suggestion.summary: A starter prompt or follow-up the user can pick instead of typing.
use: Empty chat: Layout=card, 4 tasks the assistant does well
Under the input or after an answer: Layout=chip for follow-ups
Next to content for one known task (summarize, suggest a reply)
avoid: Filters and selections: use Chip
A command that runs at once with no prompt: use a Button with sparkles
anatomy: Label: the prompt, starting with a verb
rules: Starters come from real user tasks, never generic examples
Follow-ups: 2-4 chips, only when the next step is predictable
Click fills the input; follow-up chips send at once
Label is short: "Summarize open invoices"
a11y: Each Suggestion is a button named by its Label
Reachable with Tab; focus shows the border/ring focus ring
Prompt Suggestion.code: Vercel AI SDK + AI Elements, or assistant-ui.

AI Review Bar.summary: Floating bar for reviewing AI edits in a document or form one by one: position, previous and next, accept or reject, and accept or reject all.
use: AI edits in a document
A form AI filled from a file
Bulk AI categorization to review
avoid: One suggestion inline: use AI Suggestion
An action the AI wants to run: use Tool Call
Unsaved form changes: use Save Bar
anatomy: Navigation: previous and next Button Icons
Reject all and Accept all (Show bulk actions)
rules: Each suggestion shows inline as AI Suggestion; the bar moves between them
Keyboard: Tab next, Enter accept, Backspace reject
Accept all asks once when the changes are many
Floats at the bottom center of the document until all are reviewed
Accepted changes can be undone; at the end the bar sums up and leaves
a11y: role="toolbar" with aria-label "Review suggestions"
The position is announced politely as it changes; focus moves to the current suggestion
Shortcuts show in Tooltips with Kbd
AI Review Bar.code: custom toolbar on shadcn Button; suggestions from Tiptap track changes or a diff of the form state.

Background Job.summary: A task that runs in the background (export, import, bulk send, report): name, progress with count and time left, Cancel; Download when done, Retry when failed.
use: Exports and imports that take more than about 10 seconds
Bulk actions on many records
Reports the server builds
avoid: Short reloads of a region: use Loading Overlay
A file the person uploads: use File Item
A short note that something started: use Toast
A goal against a target: use Progress Card
anatomy: Icon tile: what the job does (download, upload, send)
Title: ui/label, the job and format ("Export invoices (CSV)")
Status (State=running): count and time left; Result (State=done): what is ready; Error (State=error): where it failed; body/small, muted
Action: Cancel Button Icon while running; Download when done; Retry when failed
rules: Status, Result and Error are separate texts for the three States, so switching State never shows the wrong line
Running shows count and time left ("1,240 of 3,000 · about 2 min left"); an indeterminate bar when the total is unknown
Done offers the result (Download) and stays until dismissed
Failed says where it stopped ("Stopped at row 1,241: invalid date") and offers Retry
Stack jobs in a panel or a corner, newest on top; people keep working
Notify when it finishes if they left the page
a11y: The bar has role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext ("1,240 of 3,000")
Done and failed are announced in a polite live region ("Export ready")
Cancel is named with the job ("Cancel export invoices"); failed status is text plus an icon
Background Job.code: custom row: shadcn Progress and Button; job status by polling or server-sent events.

Badge List.summary: A few tags on one line with +N for the rest.
use: Category, format and region of a dataset, an article or a job
Labels under a page title
Tags in a card or a table row with limited space
avoid: Filters people remove: use Chip
One status: use Badge or Status Dot
Choosing tags: use a multi Select or a Combobox
anatomy: Tags slot: Badges (outline for neutral labels)
+N Badge (Show more, exposed): secondary, opens the full list
rules: Show 2-4 tags, then +N
One or two words per tag, sentence case
Status colors only when the tag means a status
Same order everywhere (type, frequency, region)
a11y: Code as a list (ul) with a label ("Tags")
+N is a button that names the hidden tags in its Tooltip or Popover
Tags that link to a listing are links, not buttons
Badge List.code: <ul class="flex gap-1.5"> of Badges; +N as a Popover trigger.

Model Picker.summary: A compact model picker in the Prompt Input Tools slot or a chat header; opens a menu of Model Options.
use: Users really choose between cost, speed or data rules
Products that offer 2-4 models
Chat header of a full chat page, when the choice applies to the whole conversation
avoid: One sensible model: pick it for the user and leave the selector out
Choosing a value in a form: use Select
anatomy: Menu of Model Options: Name, Description, optional Badge, check on the selected one
rules: Describe models by what they are good for, not by version numbers
2-4 Model Options; the default first
Description states the trade-off in one line: quality, speed, cost
a11y: Trigger is a button with aria-haspopup and a name like "Model: Acme Pro"
Arrow keys move in the menu, Enter selects, Esc closes and returns focus
The selected option has a check and aria-checked, not color alone
Model Picker.code: AI Elements (model select, task, artifact) or custom on DropdownMenu, Badge, Card.

Uptime Bars.summary: Uptime history of one service: 90 daily bars, oldest on the left, each colored by the state of that day, with an optional "90 days ago" / "Today" caption row.
use: Under each service of a public status page (Service Status Row Show bars)
A health panel in admin that shows the last 90 days
Any daily availability history of an integration or job
avoid: A trend of a number over time: use a Chart or Sparkline
Today's status only: use Service Status Row without bars
Progress toward a goal: use Progress
anatomy: Bars: 90 Uptime Day instances (State=operational, degraded, outage, maintenance, no-data), FILL width
Caption row (Show labels): Start label "90 days ago", End label "Today", ui/caption, muted
rules: Always 90 days, oldest left, today right; the same period on every row of a page
Select a nested Uptime Day to set its State; keep the real degraded and outage days
Days before a service existed are no-data, not operational
Each day with an incident links to it; the tooltip says the date, the state and the incident title
Show labels on every row of a status page, or once under the last row
a11y: Color is never the only signal: each day has a tooltip and an accessible label ("3 Oct 2026: degraded")
The uptime % is also given as text next to the name
The bar row is a list; keyboard users reach days with incidents
Uptime Bars.code: custom: a flex row of 90 bars (flex-1 h-7 rounded-sm, bg by state) with a shadcn Tooltip per day; data from your status provider.

Pager Link.summary: Previous / next link at the end of a docs page or article: a bordered card with a caption and an arrow, then the title of the linked page.
use: The end of a docs page, before the footer (Block / Docs Page Footer)
Moving through the articles of a guide or a course in order
Previous and next post at the end of a blog article
avoid: Pages of a table or list: use Pagination
Steps of a flow or form: use Stepper
Related links that are not in a sequence: use Post Card Layout=compact or List Item
anatomy: Caption row: chevron icon on the side of the Direction and the caption text set by variant ("Previous" / "Next"), ui/caption, muted
Title: title of the linked page, ui/label
rules: Direction=previous on the left, Direction=next on the right, in two equal columns
The caption text comes from the Direction ("Previous" / "Next"); override the text layer directly only to localize it
Title is the exact title of the linked page, never "Next page"
On the first page show only Next, on the last only Previous; keep the empty column so Next stays on the right
The whole card is the link: State=hover and State=focus
a11y: Wrap both links in a nav with aria-label="Previous and next page"
The link text reads "Previous: <title>"; the chevron is aria-hidden
Focus shows the focus ring (State=focus)
Pager Link.code: custom: <a> card (rounded-xl border p-4 hover:bg-accent focus-visible:ring) with lucide ChevronLeft / ChevronRight, inside a <nav>.

Image Figure.summary: An image with a caption under it and an optional credit, for galleries, articles and docs.
use: Gallery grids of photos with captions (Block / Gallery Grid)
Screenshots and photos in articles and docs that need a caption
Press and case study pages that credit the photographer
avoid: An image without caption: use Image Placeholder
A number with a label: use Figure
A product or post with a title and actions: use Product Card or Post Card
anatomy: Image: exposed Image Placeholder, set its Ratio (16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 21:9); Show caption off
Caption: what or where it is, body/small, muted
rules: Set the ratio on the nested Image Placeholder; put the photo as an image fill on it
One caption style and one line length per gallery; captions are short phrases without a period
Credit only when the source must be named (stock, press, a photographer)
In masonry galleries mix 4:3 and 3:4 per column; keep column widths equal
a11y: Use <figure> and <figcaption>; the image still has alt text that says what it shows
Do not repeat the caption word for word in the alt text
Caption contrast is at least 4.5:1

Icon Tile.summary: A rounded square holding one Lucide icon, the marker for a feature, step, stat or bento card.
use: Feature grids and benefit lists on marketing pages
Bento cards and "How it works" rows that lead with an icon
Help categories, support options and contact methods
Stats or KPI cards that need a small visual anchor
avoid: Status or meaning: use Badge or Status Dot (the tile is decorative)
Clickable icon buttons: use Button Icon
People or companies: use Avatar or Logo
Numbered steps where order matters: use Feature Item Marker=number
anatomy: Tile: rounded square, Size=default 40 (radius/md), sm 32 (radius/md), lg 48 (radius/lg)
Icon (Icon swap): Lucide icon, 20 / 16 / 24 px, default Icon/sparkles
Style=brand: icon-tile/brand-bg fill (background/primary at 10% light, 20% dark), icon-tile/brand-fg icon (foreground/brand)
Style=gradient: linear icon-tile/gradient-start to icon-tile/gradient-end, foreground/primary icon
Style=outline: no fill, border/default ring (border-width/DEFAULT), foreground/muted icon
rules: One Style per grid; gradient for one hero feature or one highlighted step only
Same Size across a grid: default in feature grids, sm in dense lists, lg in bento cards
Pick icons from one family (Lucide) with the same stroke weight
brand and gradient follow the theme: violet in Showcase, near black in Default, blue in Corporate
a11y: The icon is decorative next to a title: aria-hidden on the svg
Icon contrast 3:1 or more in every mode (lowest: gradient start 4.2:1 in Showcase)
Never the only carrier of meaning; the title says what it is
Icon Tile.code: ; brand: bg-[var(--icon-tile-brand-bg)] text-brand; gradient: bg-linear-to-br from-[var(--icon-tile-gradient-start)] to-[var(--icon-tile-gradient-end)] text-primary-foreground; outline: border text-muted-foreground.

Background / Grid.summary: A decorative square grid of 1 px lines behind a hero or feature section, fading toward the edges.
use: Behind a centered hero headline (with Background / Glow)
Behind a feature or developer-tool section that needs a technical feel
Behind a CTA band
avoid: More than one decorative device on a page: pick Grid, Dots, Glow or Beam
Behind dense content, tables or forms
Inside cards or app screens
anatomy: Lines: one vector of 1 px lines in border/default at 60%, 40 px cells, 1920 x 1080, centered and clipped
Fade mask (Fade): an alpha mask with a radial fade, scales with the frame; off shows the full grid
rules: Put it at the back of the section: first child, Absolute position, constraints Left and right + Top (or Scale)
Default size 1440 x 800; stretch it up to 1920 x 1080 and the cells stay square
No text or meaning inside; it is decoration only
Keep body copy short over it; muted text crossing a line reads 4.3:1 on that pixel row in Light
a11y: Decorative: aria-hidden, no role
Text over it keeps 4.5:1 against the plain page between the lines
Respect forced colors: hide it in high contrast mode
Background / Grid.code: Absolutely positioned div behind the section: bg-[linear-gradient(to_right,var(--border)_1px,transparent_1px),linear-gradient(to_bottom,var(--border)_1px,transparent_1px)] bg-[size:40px_40px] opacity-60 with mask-image: radial-gradient(ellipse at center, black 40%, transparent 100%) (Fade); aria-hidden.

Background / Dots.summary: A decorative dot pattern (1.5 px dots, 24 px pitch) behind a hero, feature or CTA section, fading toward the edges.
use: Behind a hero or a feature section as a quieter alternative to the grid
Behind a CTA band or a testimonial highlight
avoid: More than one decorative device on a page
Behind dense content, tables or forms
Inside cards or app screens
anatomy: Dots: one vector of round dots in foreground/muted at 50%, 24 px pitch, 1920 x 1080, centered and clipped
Fade mask (Fade): an alpha mask with a radial fade; off shows the full pattern
rules: Put it at the back of the section: first child, Absolute position, constraints Left and right + Top (or Scale)
Default size 1440 x 800; the pitch stays even up to 1920 x 1080
No text inside; decoration only
a11y: Decorative: aria-hidden, no role
Text over it keeps 4.5:1: the dots are 1.5 px and low contrast
Background / Dots.code: Absolutely positioned div: bg-[radial-gradient(var(--muted-foreground)_0.75px,transparent_0.75px)] bg-[size:24px_24px] opacity-50, mask-image radial-gradient for Fade; aria-hidden.

Background / Glow.summary: One large blurred ellipse in the primary color (gradient/brand-glow) that lights a hero, a product shot or a CTA corner.
use: Position=top: a soft light above a hero headline
Position=center: behind a product screenshot, a pricing card or a device frame
Position=bottom-right: a corner accent in a CTA band or footer lead-in
avoid: Body text on the glow core: muted text needs a background within about 6% of the page
More than one glow per page (Grid + Glow together count as one hero treatment)
App screens and dashboards
anatomy: Glow: one ellipse with the gradient/brand-glow style (background/primary 35% to transparent) and blur/3xl, constraints Scale
rules: Put it at the back of the section, above Grid or Dots if you combine them, Absolute position, constraints Left and right + Top (or Scale)
The color follows the theme: violet in Showcase, gray in Default, blue in Corporate
Keep the subtitle and body copy outside the bright part; top is tuned so a centered hero subtitle sits on the plain page
a11y: Decorative: aria-hidden
Measured in the hero example: subtitle on the plain page (4.74:1 Showcase Light, 7.85:1 Showcase Dark); headline 14:1 or more
Background / Glow.code: Absolutely positioned div: size and position per variant, rounded-full bg-[radial-gradient(closest-side,color-mix(in_oklab,var(--primary)_35%,transparent),transparent)] blur-3xl; aria-hidden; pointer-events-none.

Background / Beam.summary: Two or three thin diagonal light beams in the primary color entering from the top, a subtle accent for a hero or CTA band.
use: Behind a left-aligned hero (Hero Split): the beams sit in the middle and right
Behind a CTA band or a launch announcement
avoid: Behind centered body text
With another decorative device on the same page
App screens
anatomy: Beam 1-3: rectangles rotated 35 degrees, linear background/primary to gradient/primary-transparent at 12-22% alpha, blur/2xl, constraints Scale
rules: Put it at the back of the section: Absolute position, constraints Left and right + Top (or Scale)
Keep body text off the bright upper end of a beam
The color follows the theme
a11y: Decorative: aria-hidden
Background / Beam.code: Absolutely positioned divs rotated 35deg with bg-linear-to-b from-primary/20 to-transparent blur-2xl inside an overflow-hidden wrapper; aria-hidden.
